_comment: Gate classes for #915 Wave 4. class: product (a user-visible claim) | contract (a repo-internal wiring or shape claim) | hygiene (a tighten-only ratchet over the test suite's own meta-quality). rung: the ladder rung the gate is enforced at (docs/dev-environment.md#the-local-gate-loop). door: WHERE the gate is answerable, in the same vocabulary the law's rules use (.governance/law/lib/rule.mjs DOORS) — hook (rungs 0-1, the local hooks, where the author still holds the change), window (rung 2, CI on the pull request and the law's front page), owner (rung 3 and above, the scheduled lanes the owner reads). Rung and door are two views of one fact and the test holds them in step. Cost economics (#576) are a tiebreaker WITHIN a door, never a reason to move one. Enforced by scripts/ci/gate-classes.test.mjs.

test:affected.why: The affected packages' tests — the gate that actually catches breakage, and the wall clock every other rung-1 gate hides behind.

test:qualities.why: The U/T-series product quality suites over the built packages.

design:gallery.why: Pixel baselines for the design gallery. No CI job owns it (it needs a downloaded browser), so rung 1 is its only enforcement.

knip.why: Repo-wide dead-export sweep. At 28.8 s it needs a 3.9% hit rate against the 12.3-minute round trip, and it clears it.

typecheck:affected.why: Types on the diff. The full typecheck stays in CI, which recomputes it authoritatively.

scripts:test.why: The unit tests for every gate script. A broken gate is a silent gate.

test:ratchet:unit.why: The floors ratchet's own unit tests (deletion and missing-key cases).

check:reachability.why: Every share surface must be reachable from a route a user can get to.

format:check.why: Formatting. The formatter is the contract; a reformat in review is noise nobody reads.

turbo:lint.why: Per-package lint, which the root oxlint pass does not cover.

lint.why: oxlint over the tree at 2.5 s — the cheapest gate in the set by hit rate.

lint:hermes-surface.why: A Hermes array-surface gap crashes the phone, and the phone is the product.

test:claims.why: Claims, nightly and release wiring: a lane the report claims must be a lane a workflow schedules. Renamed from test:matrix with tests/claims.json (#915 Wave 3).

lint:evidence-mapping.why: An evidence file naming no claim, or a claim whose lane writes no evidence, is a rung-2 lint failure rather than a banner on the report (#915 Wave 3).

test:report:smoke.why: The report generator must render every section from the fixture root.

lint:product.why: The bundle: 38 sub-second contract/product gates in one node process under one gate name (scripts/lint-product.mjs).

test:governance-shell.why: The coverage-scope directive's self-test plus its live check — the enforcing test for a constitutional directive.

lint:node-version.why: The pinned Node. Warns locally, fatal under CI, where the claim is real.

lint:test-reachability.why: Every *.test.* / *.spec.* file in the tree is reached by a vitest project, a package.json runner list or a Playwright config. A test nothing runs is a green suite that proves nothing (#931).

lint:no-nul-bytes.why: A raw NUL in a source file makes git call it binary, and every diff in it becomes unreviewable. Three files reached main that way before this gate (#931).

lint:packages.why: Monorepo package hygiene (sherif): duplicate deps and mismatched versions across workspaces.

lint:tsconfigs.why: tsconfig shape across the workspace — one composite graph, no ad-hoc overrides.

lint:turbo-cache.why: A turbo `outputs` entry naming a tracked path makes the task its own input, and turbo silently stops caching.

lint:path-filters.why: `skipped` counts as a pass, so a path no filter names merges green and unexercised (G-filter-inverse).

test:ratchet.why: Coverage and mutation floors are up-only against the merge base. Up-only floors are a contract, not a suite ratchet.

lint:css.why: The CSS class contract between the blueprint apps and the design package.

lint:site-tokens.why: The site's tokens must be the ones lowered from @centraid/design, not a second copy.

lint:mobile-design.why: Design-token consumption on the mobile surface.

lint:mobile-testids.why: E-unfakeable: a device flow may only assert on a declared testID.

lint:list-anchoring.why: A virtualized list that anchors by default swallows rows arriving from another device (#903).

lint:logical-insets.why: Logical inset properties, never physical ones, so RTL is correct by construction.

lint:hairline.why: Hairline borders come from the token, not from a literal that breaks at 3x density.

lint:design-md.why: The structure of the rulebook itself, so DESIGN.md stays machine-readable.

lint:e2e-flows.why: A flow may not assert on a marker every screen draws.

lint:e2e-wiring.why: An owner that no lane schedules is a claim with no evidence.

lint:app-conformance.why: A launcher tile that reaches no screen — buildLauncherItems drops an unmapped app id silently.

lint:e2e-claims.why: Every device flow must name what merges wrongly if it passes when it should not.

lint:seat-verbs.why: Seat verbs must match the seat registry; a verb no seat declares reaches no screen.

check:na-cells.why: A deliberate n/a cell carries a kind, a citation and a review date; the report renders it as n/a-with-reason. It pins a claims-file row to a reason, so it is a contract rather than a suite ratchet.

check:mobile-suite-budgets.why: A mobile suite budget must track its observed p95; slack is a failure.

lint:engine-conformance.why: Shared engines conform to their declared contracts.

lint:ledgers.why: The one validator over the four merged ledgers (#915 Wave 4): direction, per-section waiver scope, issue-and-expiry, and the two derived mirrors. Pure file reading against the merge base, so it is a rung-1 contract gate.

lint:law-registry.why: One law, one home: every law in the registry is wired to a real enforcer.

lint:protocol-routes.why: The protocol route table: a declared route with no handler, or a handler with no route.

lint:acp-min-versions.why: ACP minimum versions: a backend claiming a protocol level it cannot serve.

lint:aria-labels.why: Accessibility is user-facing, so it is product, not meta-quality.

lint:container-opacity.why: The container-opacity rule from DESIGN.md; opacity on a container flattens everything inside it.

lint:motion-rule.why: The motion rule from DESIGN.md: durations and easings come from the tokens.

lint:quality-knobs.why: A governed knob may only tighten against the merge base.

check:ui-receipt.why: A UI-touching diff must carry a UI receipt.

test:quarantine.why: A quarantined test must be declared, attributed and unexpired. The expiry is the contract; the count is not ratcheted.

test:advisory-expiry.why: A step that announces it will never fail must carry an owner, an issue and a date by which someone decides.

test:accessibility.why: The accessibility contract — the behaviours a screen reader depends on.

lockfile:lint.why: Lockfile shape: a lockfile that drifts from package.json makes every other gate's answer conditional.

security:lifecycle.why: Supply chain: lifecycle scripts reach the user's machine.

security:unsafe-edges.why: Supply chain: unsafe dependency edges reach the user's machine.

lint:ci-egress.why: Every workflow that runs dependency code must constrain its egress or be ledgered.

test:comment-density.why: A down-only per-file comment-density pin over the whole tree. It protects the suite from the agents; it cannot prove the phone works. 10.2 s, the most expensive non-test gate, and it had NO CI job at all before #915 — weekly on main is strictly more enforcement than it had.

test:hygiene-ratchet.why: Down-only assertion-matcher family counts (toBeTruthy/toBeFalsy, the non-negated toHaveBeenCalled family). A standing count over the tree, so a weekly run on main sees exactly what a push run would.

test:sleep-inventory.why: A down-only budget on fixed sleeps in tests. Standing inventory; weekly on main loses latency, not coverage.

test:skip-inventory.why: The skip budget, split out of test:ratchet so the up-only floors half stays at rung 1. Standing inventory over the tree.

test:env-red.why: The deterministically-environment-red inventory and its down-only budget. Standing inventory; the budget must equal the discovered count either way.

lint:type-floor.why: The 11px type floor. Named by #915 as hygiene and moved, but it is the one gate in this class whose red IS user-visible (an unreadable label ships), and it reads no ledger — a pure source scan. The tradeoff is recorded in docs/decisions.md: detection moves from every push to within 7 days on main.

lint:schema-export.why: The vault-schema/portable-export fingerprint. Its enforcing comparison is standing (fingerprint vs source), so a weekly run on main detects the same drift; only the diff-scoped 'touch the export owner in the same PR' hint is lost. Tradeoff recorded in docs/decisions.md.

check:mobile-native-state.why: 30.5 s, the second-largest non-test pole. ci.yml's mobile-smoke job already runs it on exactly the diffs that matter (ci.yml #782 note); paying it on every push duplicated a rung-2 answer.

lint:journey-ledger.why: The journey ledger's own shape (#927): every entry keyed surface/journey/volume/hardware, naming a declared volume and hardware, its spans and a consumer that exists — and no surviving reference to the five files it replaced.

governance.why: The governance directives, through the stamped entry point. The pre-commit hook runs them; `bun run governance` is the name a developer or an agent calls the same run by.

governance:law:test.why: The law's own rule and generator suites. It rides scripts:test, which check:push names at rung 1 and ci.yml re-runs at rung 2, so the RuleTester cases are not enforced by a developer's hook alone.
